cards.label: Buy back your own stock
pros: Immediate lift to the share price
cons: Spends cash the turnaround may need
Does nothing to the operating story
cards.consequence: NovaTech retires shares in the open market; the tape ticks up.

cards.label: Buy back your own debt
pros: Can book a gain if bonds are cheap
cons: Quiet — the market may not notice
cards.consequence: Bonds are lifted below par; leverage eases a notch.

cards.label: Sell new shares for cash
pros: Buys time on the balance sheet
cons: Reads as an admission of weakness
cards.consequence: A follow-on offering lands cash and a weaker tape.

cards.label: Pay debt off outright
pros: Cuts the interest bill every quarter after
cons: Spends cash on a problem nobody may be asking about
Opportunity cost vs. the fight in public
cards.consequence: Principal is retired; the interest line shrinks next quarter.

cards.label: Cut costs structurally
pros: Easy to sell as fiscal discipline
cards.consequence: A freeze and a round of cuts free up cash; the floor goes quiet.

cards.label: Raise prices
cons: Looks opportunistic if the story is fragile
cards.consequence: List prices move up; a few accounts push back.

cards.label: Pay key people to stay
pros: The only card that really moves morale
Keeps the campaign's operators in their seats
cons: Does not fix debt or the tape
cards.consequence: Stay bonuses hit payroll; the flight-risk list shortens.

cards.label: Change who's in charge
pros: Seizes initiative in a slate fight
Lifts confidence that the thesis has owners
cards.consequence: A new slate is named; the org chart redraws itself overnight.

cards.label: Win the public narrative
pros: Speaks to proxy advisers and the press
cons: Changes nothing about how the business actually runs
cards.consequence: The open letter and roadshow land; the tape hears a story, not a number.

cards.label: Push for a quick operating win
cards.consequence: A 90-day sprint posts a modest print; people are tired.

cards.label: Invest in a real product improvement
pros: Durable vs. a one-quarter price pop
cons: Squeezes margin while it is being built
cards.consequence: R&D gets a real budget; the roadmap stops being a slide.

cards.label: Buy a smaller rival or disruptor
pros: Biggest single swing: innovation and share
cons: Stitching the companies creates integration risk
cards.consequence: The challenger is bought; two stacks now have to become one.

cards.label: Partner instead of buy
pros: Some of an acquisition's reach without the price tag
cards.consequence: A partnership is signed; two roadmaps now have to meet in the middle.

cards.label: Force the pieces to actually work together
pros: Converts integration risk into margin and revenue
cons: Needs a live deal or partnership first
cards.consequence: A war-room on integration actually ships a combined SKU.

cards.label: Sell off an old business line
pros: Raises cash and de-risks the sheet
cons: Shrinks revenue and share right now
cards.consequence: The declining unit is sold; the remaining company is smaller and cleaner.

cards.label: Clean up governance and regulatory exposure
cards.consequence: Audits and controls land; the counsel's file gets thinner.

knockOnRules.news: Morale collapse hits innovation and revenue.
Innovation proof starts lifting confidence on its own.
